name: The Amalfi Coast
tagline: Vertiginous cliffs, pastel villages and impossibly blue sea.
whenBlurb: May-June and September-October are warm, calm and golden; avoid the crowded July-August heat and the November-March shutdown, when many hotels close.

ourTake.lede: The Amalfi Coast is best travelled by boat, not by that white-knuckle coast road, hire a gozzo for the day and you'll understand the place in a way the bus tours never will. Positano is the postcard but Ravello, high above the sea, is where you'll actually want to stay: cooler, quieter, and with the two great villa gardens. Come in May or late September; July and August turn the road into a car park and the beaches into a scrum.
ourTake.comeIf: You want long lunches over the sea, a boat to Capri, and cliffside towns with nowhere to rush to.
ourTake.skipIf: You want big-resort beaches, nightlife, or an easy step-free trip, the coast is all stairs and switchbacks.

guide.lede: Where to stay, what to do, where to eat, and where the night goes, grouped by price, every address earned by a name worth trusting.

items.name: Il San Pietro di Positano
credentials: MICHELIN Three Keys (2025), the Amalfi Coast's only Three-Key hotel
The Leading Hotels of the World
items.description: Carved into the cliff itself, invisible from the road, the coast's most complete idea of privacy and drama.

items.name: Le Sirenuse
credentials: The Leading Hotels of the World (since 1970)
items.description: The Sersale family's 1951 house, hand-painted tiles, treasured antiques, and Positano's most famous terrace.

items.name: Caruso, A Belmond Hotel, Amalfi Coast
items.description: An 11th-century palace on the cliff-edge of Ravello, with an infinity pool that seems to pour into the sea.

items.name: J.K. Place Capri
items.description: Just 22 rooms of quiet, design-led perfection above Marina Grande, beauty without a trace of ostentation.

items.name: Palazzo Avino
credentials: The Leading Hotels of the World
items.description: A rose-pink 12th-century villa on the Ravello ridge, 'the pink palace', timeless and serene.

items.name: Hotel Santa Caterina
credentials: The Leading Hotels of the World
items.description: A family-owned grande dame among blooming terraces, with a cliff-lift down to a seawater pool.

items.name: Borgo Santandrea
items.description: A dazzling cliffside newcomer of hand-made majolica and private sea terraces, the coast's most talked-about opening.

items.name: Villa TreVille
credentials: The Leading Hotels of the World
items.description: Franco Zeffirelli's former private estate, three villas of theatrical, deeply personal glamour above the sea.

items.name: Capri Palace Jumeirah
items.description: An art-filled Anacapri palace with the island's most serious spa, and the world's only starred beach club.

items.name: Hotel La Palma Capri, an Oetker Collection Hotel
items.description: Capri's oldest hotel, reborn by Oetker, the island's historic address returned to full glamour.

items.name: Grand Hotel Excelsior Vittoria
credentials: The Leading Hotels of the World
items.description: A five-generation family palace on the cliff above Sorrento's marina, with citrus gardens and Caruso's own suite.

items.name: Monastero Santa Rosa Hotel & Spa
items.description: A 17th-century Dominican monastery on a private headland, hushed, garden-wrapped and utterly serene.

items.name: Casa Angelina
credentials: The Leading Hotels of the World
items.description: A pure-white, art-filled cliff house above Praiano, minimalist, modern and blissfully quiet.

items.name: Capri Tiberio Palace
items.description: A jewel-box design hotel a short walk from the Piazzetta, colourful, cultured and quietly glamorous.

items.name: Hotel Punta Tragara
items.description: A Le Corbusier-designed terrace hotel gazing straight at the Faraglioni sea stacks, Capri's signature view.

items.name: Caesar Augustus
credentials: The Leading Hotels of the World
items.description: A cliff-top former villa 300m above the sea in quiet Anacapri, an infinity terrace over the whole bay of Naples.

items.name: Hotel Le Agavi
items.description: A terraced hillside garden hotel with a private funicular down to its own beach club, Positano without the crush.

items.name: Hotel Marincanto
items.description: A cliffside garden hotel with steps straight down to the beach, classic Positano at a gentler pitch.

items.name: Villa Franca
items.description: A top-of-town house with a rooftop pool looking straight down the length of Positano.

items.name: Hotel Villa Cimbrone
credentials: Gardens rated a top Amalfi sight, MICHELIN Green Guide
items.description: An 11th-century villa built around the Terrace of Infinity, a garden hotel of rare, literary romance.

items.name: Villa Marina Capri Hotel & Spa
items.description: A discreet, family-run villa hotel with a fine spa, a short stroll from the Piazzetta.

items.name: Bellevue Syrene 1820
items.description: A neoclassical villa on the Sorrento cliff-edge since 1820, frescoed, antique-filled and grandly romantic.

items.name: Don Alfonso 1890 (Relais)
items.description: A tiny Relais above the two gulfs, wrapped around one of the south's most celebrated kitchens.

items.name: Hotel Poseidon
items.description: A family-run Positano institution with a pool terrace and a warmth that keeps guests returning for decades.

items.name: Palazzo Murat
items.description: An 18th-century Bourbon palace around a bougainvillea courtyard, steps from the beach and the Duomo.

items.name: Hotel Miramalfi
items.description: A cliff-clinging Amalfi hotel with a seawater pool cut into the rock, honest comfort with a real sea view.

items.name: The Amalfi Coast Drive (Strada Statale 163)
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Costiera Amalfitana
items.description: The serpentine coast road threads cliff-edge above a cobalt sea, past lemon terraces and pastel villages, and it is deliberately, gloriously slow. Hand it to a private driver so the whole family can watch the view instead of the hairpins, and stop wherever a belvedere catches the light.

items.name: A Private Boat Day Along the Coast
items.description: The coast reads entirely differently from the water, you swim off the boat in hidden coves, glide under the Furore bridge, and reach beaches no road serves. A chartered gozzo or motor yacht with a skipper is the discreet, unhurried way to see it, with a private lunch stop and shade for the elders.

items.name: Positano, Spiaggia Grande
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Costiera Amalfitana
items.description: The wide crescent of dark pebbles at the foot of the vertical village is the beating heart of Positano, framed by the tumble of pastel houses climbing the cliff. Book sunbeds at a chic beach club for the day and let ferries and water taxis buzz in and out while you watch.

items.name: Fornillo Beach & the Cliffside Path
items.description: A short, immensely pretty cliff walk from Marina Grande leads to Fornillo, a quieter cove with crystal water that feels worlds away from the summer crowds. It is the calmer beach for a slow honeymoon afternoon or families wanting space from the main scene.

items.name: Church of Santa Maria Assunta
items.description: Positano's icon, a majolica dome of yellow, green and blue tiles blazing against the sky and sea, just steps from the beach. Inside is a revered 13th-century Byzantine Black Madonna, and beneath, a medieval crypt worth the quiet detour.

items.name: Path of the Gods (Sentiero degli Dei)
items.description: The legendary ridge traverse runs high above the coast from Bomerano to Nocelle, an ancient mule track with unbroken views to the sea and the silhouette of Capri. Walk it east-to-west so Positano stays in front of you; a private guide can pace it gently and arrange a car at both ends.

items.name: Amalfi, Cathedral of Sant'Andrea
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Costiera Amalfitana
items.description: A dramatic sweep of steps rises to a striped Arab-Norman-Byzantine facade that crowns the whole town. Inside rest the relics of Saint Andrew, and the adjoining Cloister of Paradise, a Moorish garden of slender white columns, is one of the coast's most serene corners.

items.name: Museo della Carta (Paper Museum)
items.description: Housed in a cave-like 13th-century paper mill, the oldest in Europe, this small museum shows how Amalfi made the handmade cotton paper that built its medieval trading power. The guided tour, with the old water-wheels still turning, delights curious children and grandparents alike.

items.name: Valle delle Ferriere Nature Reserve
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Costiera Amalfitana
items.description: A cool, green ravine of streams, waterfalls and giant prehistoric Woodwardia ferns, living fossils, with the ivy-clad ruins of 12th-century ironworks emerging from the vegetation. A gentle three-hour escape from the heat and the crowds, a small entry fee, best with a nature guide.

items.name: Ravello, Villa Rufolo & Its Gardens
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Costiera Amalfitana
items.description: A 13th-century palace whose terraced gardens so moved Wagner that he set Parsifal's magic garden here. During the summer Ravello Festival, concerts play on a stage cantilevered over the cliff with only sea and sky behind the orchestra, pure theatre for a romantic evening.

items.name: Ravello Festival Concerts
items.description: From July into September, Ravello, 'the city of music', stages classical concerts in Villa Rufolo's gardens, the famous stage floating above the Gulf of Salerno. A sunset chamber recital or grand orchestral night here is one of the coast's most memorable indulgences.

items.name: Villa Cimbrone & the Terrace of Infinity
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Costiera Amalfitana
items.description: A romantic garden ending in the Terrazza dell'Infinito, a marble-busted belvedere that Gore Vidal called the most beautiful view in the world, the coast falling away 350 metres to the sea below. Go early or late for the light, and for the honeymoon photograph everyone wants.

items.name: Emerald Grotto (Grotta dello Smeraldo)
items.description: A sea cave where sunlight filtering through an underwater fissure turns the whole cavern a glowing emerald green, its floor spiked with stalactites and stalagmites. Reached by lift from the coast road or by boat, it is a short, magical stop, an easy wonder for all ages.

items.name: Fiordo di Furore
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Costiera Amalfitana
items.description: A slim fjord slicing into the cliffs, spanned high above by the coast-road bridge and hiding a tiny pebble beach and cluster of old fishermen's houses at its foot. Every summer divers leap from the 30-metre bridge in an international championship; best admired from the water on a boat day.

items.name: Atrani, Italy's Smallest Town
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Costiera Amalfitana
items.description: A single, near-perfect fishing village of stacked houses and a tiny piazza opening onto the sea, just around the headland from Amalfi yet almost untouched by its crowds. Come for a slow, authentic dinner where locals still outnumber visitors.

items.name: Praiano & Marina di Praia
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Costiera Amalfitana
items.description: Widely called the coast's most romantic village for its sunsets and its double view, the bay of Positano on one side, Capri on the other. Below, the sliver of Marina di Praia beach tucks between cliffs, and the seaside path to Grotta dell'Africana makes a lovely evening walk.

items.name: Vietri sul Mare, the Ceramics Town
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Costiera Amalfitana
items.description: The 'Capital of Ceramics,' where five centuries of hand-painted majolica spill from every workshop in bold Mediterranean colour. Commission a bespoke dinner service or tiles, and see the Solimene factory's extraordinary curved facade and the tiled Villa Comunale.

items.name: Li Galli Islands
items.description: Three private islets between Positano and Capri, mythologised as the home of Homer's sirens and once owned by dancers Nureyev and Massine. You cannot land, but circling them by boat and swimming in the clear water around Gallo Lungo is a highlight of any coast cruise.

items.name: Lemon Grove & Limoncello Experience
items.description: On terraces cut vertically into the cliff, family farms grow the prized Sfusato Amalfitano lemon, huge, fragrant, PGI-protected. Walk the pergolas, pick your own fruit, distil a bottle of limoncello to take home, and taste lemon cake in the shade; children love the ritual.

items.name: A Private Cooking Class
items.description: Learn to make fresh pasta, seafood or classic Campanian dishes in a hillside kitchen or amid the lemon groves, then eat what you cooked over a long lunch. Hosts happily build a fully vegetarian menu, ideal for multi-generational groups and a warm, hands-on afternoon.

items.name: Capri, The Blue Grotto (Grotta Azzurra)
items.description: Known to the Romans as Tiberius's bath, this sea cave fills with an otherworldly electric-blue light as sun refracts through the water beneath the low entrance. You lie flat in a small rowing boat to slip inside, a brief, unforgettable thrill worth timing carefully for calm sea.

items.name: Capri, The Piazzetta
items.description: The little square under its clock tower is the island's stage, where an aperitivo among the well-dressed is almost obligatory. Sit, order a drink, and watch the parade, the most stylish people-watching in the Mediterranean.

items.name: Capri, The Faraglioni
items.description: Three towering rock stacks rising from the sea off Capri's southern coast, the island's signature silhouette. Boats pass through the natural arch of the middle stack for luck; the Belvedere di Tragara above gives the classic postcard view.

items.name: Anacapri & Villa San Michele
items.description: Quieter, higher and more authentic than Capri town, Anacapri holds the villa built by Swedish doctor Axel Munthe, a house of classical antiquities opening onto a pergola and one of the island's finest sea panoramas. A calmer, cultured half-day away from the glamour.

items.name: Chairlift to Monte Solaro
items.description: A gentle single-seat chairlift floats you up over gardens and orchards to Capri's 589-metre summit in about fifteen minutes, opening a 360-degree panorama over the island, the Faraglioni, the Bay of Naples and Vesuvius. Effortless, and a highlight for those who don't want to hike.

items.name: Sorrento, Marina Grande & Villa Comunale
items.description: The old fishing quarter of Marina Grande lines the quay with characterful seafood trattorie, while up in town the Villa Comunale gardens frame a sunset view across the bay to Vesuvius, with a lift down to the water. An easy, gracious base and gateway between coast and city.

items.name: Bagni della Regina Giovanna
items.description: A natural sea pool ringed by the ruins of a Roman villa, connected to the open sea by a rocky arch, Queen Joanna's legendary bathing spot. A short walk from the road delivers a wild, uncrowded swim far from any beach club, for those who like their luxury raw.

items.name: Pompeii
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Archaeological Areas of Pompei, Herculaneum and Torre Annunziata
items.description: The Roman city frozen mid-life by the eruption of AD 79, streets, frescoed villas, a forum and plaster casts of its people, all sealed under ash for centuries. Vast and moving; go with a private archaeologist-guide early in the day, and mind the heat for elders and children.

items.name: Herculaneum (Ercolano)
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Archaeological Areas of Pompei, Herculaneum and Torre Annunziata
items.description: Smaller than Pompeii but far better preserved, buried by hot mud that carbonised and saved wooden beams, doors, even furniture, so you walk through intact multi-storey Roman houses. The quieter, more intimate ruin, easily paired with Pompeii or done on its own.

items.name: Villa Oplontis (Torre Annunziata)
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Archaeological Areas of Pompei, Herculaneum and Torre Annunziata
items.description: A sumptuous seaside villa, likely Empress Poppaea's, with some of the finest Roman wall paintings anywhere yet almost no crowds. The connoisseur's stop on the Vesuvian circuit, vivid trompe-l'oeil frescoes and a garden colonnade, all to yourself.

items.name: Mount Vesuvius
items.description: The volcano that buried Pompeii still broods over the bay, and a short walk from the car park along the crater rim rewards you with a look into its smoking mouth and a sweeping view over Naples and Capri. A driver to the upper gate makes it comfortable for the whole family.

items.name: Paestum, The Greek Temples
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Cilento and Vallo di Diano National Park with the Archaeological Sites of Paestum and Velia
items.description: Three colossal Doric temples of the 6th and 5th centuries BC, standing golden and near-complete in open meadows, among the best-preserved Greek architecture on earth, older than the Parthenon. Deeply calm and uncrowded; pair with the museum's famous Tomb of the Diver fresco.

items.name: Naples, Cappella Sansevero & the Veiled Christ
items.description: In a small Baroque chapel lies Sammartino's Cristo Velato, a marble Christ draped in a veil so translucent it seems impossible carved from stone, one of the world's great sculptures. A short, spellbinding visit at the heart of the old city; book timed tickets ahead.

items.name: Naples, Spaccanapoli & the Historic Centre
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Historic Centre of Naples
items.description: The dead-straight ancient street that literally splits old Naples, lined with churches, cloisters and the year-round nativity artisans of Via San Gregorio Armeno. Loud, alive and utterly authentic, the antidote to the coast's polish, best explored on foot with a guide and a pizza stop.

items.name: Naples, Museo Archeologico Nazionale
items.description: The treasury of everything portable dug from Pompeii and Herculaneum, the great mosaics, bronzes and frescoes, plus the Farnese marbles. Seeing it before or after the ruins makes the whole story click; a private guide keeps it to the highlights for a two-hour visit.

items.name: Nocelle Village
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Costiera Amalfitana
items.description: A tiny car-free hamlet clinging to the mountain above Positano, the eastern end of the Path of the Gods, with a handful of terrace trattorie and a plunging sea view. Descend the 1,700-odd steps to town, or simply lunch here in the hush far above the resort.

items.name: Conca dei Marini & Marina di Conca
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Costiera Amalfitana
items.description: One of the coast's smallest, most exclusive villages, wrapped around a jewel of a cove below whitewashed houses, long a discreet retreat for the international set. Come by boat for the swimming and the seclusion, and taste the local sfogliatella Santa Rosa where it was invented.

items.name: Furore, The Village That Isn't There
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Costiera Amalfitana
items.description: A 'painted village' with no real centre, its houses scattered up the mountainside and its walls covered in vivid murals, threaded by the Path of the Love (Sentiero dell'Amore). A quiet, offbeat wander for those who have already ticked the icons.

items.name: Cetara, Fishing Village & Colatura
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Costiera Amalfitana
items.description: A working tuna and anchovy port that still makes colatura di alici, the amber anchovy essence descended from Roman garum. Eat spaghetti alla colatura at a harbourside table where the fishermen land their catch, the coast's most delicious hidden authenticity.

items.name: Scala, The Oldest Town on the Coast
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Costiera Amalfitana
items.description: Facing Ravello across the valley, Scala is the coast's most ancient settlement and one of its quietest, with a medieval cathedral and paths down through chestnut woods and terraces. A restorative half-day for walkers and those seeking the coast before tourism.

items.name: Marmorata Waterfalls & the Atrani Valley Walk
items.description: The green Dragone valley behind Atrani hides old mills and small waterfalls on a gentle walk up toward Ravello, an escape into shade and birdsong minutes from the sea. An easy, pretty leg-stretch that few day-trippers ever find.

items.name: Sunset Aperitivo at a Cliff Terrace
items.description: The coast faces west, so its sunsets are a nightly event, best taken with a glass on a hotel or restaurant terrace hung over the sea. Reserve the corner table at a Michelin-starred maison or a Ravello garden bar for the evening the family will remember.

items.name: Marina di Furore & the Sea-Village Frescoes
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Costiera Amalfitana
items.description: At the mouth of the fjord sits a cluster of old monazeni, fishermen's houses built into the rock, reachable by a stair from the bridge. Photogenic and almost secret, it is the closest thing to a fishing hamlet time forgot on the whole coast.

items.name: Kayak & Swim the Sea Grottoes
items.description: Paddle a sea kayak along the base of the cliffs into little grottoes and arches, Grotta dell'Africana, Grotta del Fico, that no boat or road can reach, stopping to swim in impossibly clear water. A gentle active morning that even novices and teenagers enjoy.

items.name: Torre dello Ziro & the Amalfi–Pontone Ridge
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Costiera Amalfitana
items.description: A short climb to a lone medieval watchtower on a spur between Amalfi and Atrani, with a dizzying double-bay view and a dark Renaissance legend attached. Under an hour up from Pontone, it is the coast's best-value viewpoint for modest effort.

items.name: Sorrento Lemon & Inlaid-Wood Craft
items.description: Beyond limoncello, Sorrento is the home of intarsio, intricate inlaid marquetry, worked in family ateliers for generations. Visit a workshop and museum, commission a piece, and understand the craft heritage behind the souvenirs; a cultured pause between coast and city.

items.name: Quattro Passi
items.description: The Mellino family's cliff-top villa above the Bay of Nerano, the only three-star kitchen in all of southern Italy.

items.name: L'Olivo
items.description: Andrea Migliaccio's light, Mediterranean haute cuisine at the Capri Palace, the island's only two-star.

items.name: Don Alfonso 1890
items.description: The Iaccarino family's landmark above the two gulfs, a founding temple of modern Campanian cooking.

items.name: Torre del Saracino
items.description: Gennaro Esposito's seafront kitchen in a medieval watchtower, the coast's most decorated home-grown chef.

items.name: La Sponda
items.description: Le Sirenuse's candlelit terrace, 400 flames each night, and Positano tumbling to the sea below.

items.name: Zass
items.description: The starred kitchen of Il San Pietro, cut into the same cliff, sea light, seafood and quiet perfection.

items.name: Rossellinis
items.description: Palazzo Avino's fine-dining room high in Ravello, refined cooking with the whole coast spread beneath.

items.name: La Serra
items.description: Chef Annarumma's glass-walled room at Le Agavi, with arguably the best view of the bay in Positano.

items.name: Il Flauto di Pan
items.description: Dinner in the gardens of Villa Cimbrone, starred cooking beside the Terrace of Infinity.

items.name: Alici
items.description: Borgo Santandrea's sea-terrace kitchen, bright, ingredient-led cooking above a private cove.

items.name: Glicine
items.description: Hotel Santa Caterina's flowering-terrace dining room, looking straight out to the Amalfi sea.

items.name: Il Refettorio
items.description: Starred cooking in the old refectory of a cliff-top monastery, hushed, considered and beautifully sourced.

items.name: La Caravella dal 1959
items.description: Southern Italy's first Michelin star, in a 12th-century ducal palace, history you can taste.

items.name: Sensi
items.description: A modern, sea-facing kitchen in Amalfi town doing precise, contemporary Campanian plates.

items.name: Li Galli
items.description: Villa Franca's rooftop kitchen, named for the islands off Positano, a starred table with a panoramic sweep.

items.name: Un Piano nel Cielo
items.description: 'A floor in the sky', Casa Angelina's white-on-white starred room above quiet Praiano.

items.name: Il Riccio Restaurant & Beach Club
items.description: The world's only Michelin-starred beach club, seafood on the rocks beside the Blue Grotto.

items.name: Le Monzù
items.description: J.K. Place Capri's terrace kitchen, refined island cooking with the harbour laid out below.

items.name: Terrazza Bosquet
items.description: The starred terrace of Sorrento's grande dame, over the citrus gardens and the marina.

items.name: Il Buco
items.description: Giuseppe Aversa's kitchen in a 16th-century cellar, Campanian cooking with real personality, and famous pasta.

items.name: Lorelei
items.description: A newly-starred sea-terrace kitchen on the Sorrento cliffs, modern, bright and beautifully sited.

items.name: Relais Blu
items.description: A hillside starred room at the tip of the peninsula, with Capri floating in the window.

items.name: Antica Osteria Nonna Rosa
items.description: Family cooking of the Sorrentine hills, elevated to a star, soulful, seasonal and generous.

items.name: Next2
items.description: A stylish, sustainability-minded room on Positano's main street, modern Campanian without the grand-hotel price.

items.name: Da Adolfo
credentials: MICHELIN Guide, noted / long-standing coast institution
items.description: A ramshackle beach shack reached only by boat, grilled mozzarella on lemon leaves, and the real coast.

items.name: Lo Scoglio (Da Tommaso)
credentials: A landmark coast institution, celebrated by chefs worldwide
items.description: The beloved Bay of Nerano family trattoria, the original spaghetti alla Nerano, off its own jetty.

items.name: Il Riccio Beach Club
items.description: A white-and-blue rock terrace by the Blue Grotto, Champagne and a starred kitchen where the day slides into evening.

items.name: Franco's Bar
credentials: Part of Le Sirenuse, World's 50 Best Hotels 2025
items.description: Le Sirenuse's open-air bar suspended above Positano, a French 75 at golden hour, and the finest terrace on the coast.

items.name: Champagne & Oyster Bar, Le Sirenuse
credentials: Part of Le Sirenuse, World's 50 Best Hotels 2025
The Leading Hotels of the World
items.description: A jewel-box bar of vintage Champagne and oysters inside the coast's most storied hotel.

items.name: Anema e Core
credentials: Capri's defining nightlife institution, over 40 years
items.description: Capri's legendary taverna, Neapolitan guitars from midnight to dawn, where politicians, locals and film stars share one dance floor.

items.name: Music on the Rocks
credentials: Positano's landmark nightclub, a long-running institution
items.description: A club carved into the cliff at the end of Positano's beach, the coast's one true late-night dance floor.

plan.heading: 4 days on the Amalfi Coast, done well
plan.lede: A day-by-day shape for the trip, the pace we would set. Your advisor books the flights and the rooms; the days are yours.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: Arrive by private transfer over the coast road and settle into Le Sirenuse, with its view down the tiers of Positano.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: A slow afternoon at the hotel's Aldo's bar and pool, then a walk down to the Spiaggia Grande.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: Dinner at La Sponda at Le Sirenuse, the room lit by hundreds of candles.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: A chartered gozzo along the coast to the Li Galli islets and the grottoes below Positano.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: Lunch at Da Adolfo, reached only by boat, then swimming off the deck.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: Aperitivo at Franco's Bar, then dinner at Zass or the seafood at Chez Black on the beach.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: Drive up to Ravello for the gardens of Villa Rufolo and Villa Cimbrone's Terrace of Infinity.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: Lunch at the Belmond Caruso's cliff-edge pool, then the quiet lanes of the town.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: Dinner at Rossellinis or the Michelin table at Il Flauto di Pan, with a concert if the Ravello Festival is on.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: Private launch to Capri and the Blue Grotto before the crowds, then up to the Piazzetta.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: Lunch at Il Riccio by the Grotta Azzurra, then the chairlift to Monte Solaro above Anacapri.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: An early dinner at Da Paolino under the lemon trees before the crossing back.

items.name: Positano
items.description: The vertical, glamorous postcard town, for those who want the scene and don't mind the steps and the prices.

items.name: Ravello
items.description: High, cool and cultured above the coast, suited to travellers who prefer gardens and quiet to the beach crowd.

items.name: Amalfi & Atrani
items.description: The historic heart with its cathedral, plus tiny Atrani next door, a good central base with a real town's rhythm.

events.name: Ravello Festival
events.note: A summer-long programme of orchestral concerts and recitals on the Villa Rufolo terrace above the sea.

events.name: Regatta of the Ancient Maritime Republics
events.when: late spring (rotates; Amalfi every four years)
events.note: A costumed rowing race between Amalfi, Genoa, Pisa and Venice, with a medieval procession when Amalfi hosts.

onGround.heading: On the ground
onGround.note: Ravello sits above the crowds for serenity, Positano for the postcard; come May to June or September to avoid August gridlock, and pack flat shoes for the endless steps.

rows.label: Arriving
rows.value: Fly into Naples (NAP), then take a private car along the coast road or, far more elegantly, a helicopter or private boat transfer straight to your hotel's jetty at Positano or Ravello.

rows.label: Getting around
rows.value: Travel by private boat for coastal hops and a chauffeured car for the corniche; the cliff road is narrow and slow, so leave the driving to a local and arrive by sea where you can.

rows.label: Connectivity
rows.value: Good coverage in the towns with occasional dead spots on the cliffs and at sea; an Italy or EU eSIM plus hotel wifi covers you.

rows.label: Money
rows.value: Euro; cards work in hotels and better restaurants, but carry cash for beach clubs, boat crews and smaller trattorie, and round up for good service.

rows.label: Climate
rows.value: Late May-June and September are the sweet spot: warm sea, long light, before and after the August crush. Avoid August (peak Italian holiday, gridlocked coast road) and November-March, when many hotels and boats close.

rows.label: Flights from India
rows.value: No non-stop; the gateway is Naples. Fly one-stop via Gulf hubs (Emirates/Qatar/Etihad) into Naples, or Air India non-stop Delhi-Rome (~8.5h, 4x weekly) then ~1h to Naples. From Naples the coast is best reached by pre-arranged private car (~1.5h to Positano) or, in season, private boat transfer. Qatar Qsuite via Doha is the strongest business cabin on the routing.

rows.label: Health & safety
rows.value: No vaccinations required; routine EU standards. Very safe. The genuine hazards are the narrow, vertiginous coast road and boat transfers in rough seas, so plan drivers and timings. Tap water is potable.

rows.label: Dining, veg & Jain
rows.value: Straightforward for vegetarians; Campanian cooking is tomato-, lemon- and vegetable-led. Jain is workable at good hotels with notice. Dedicated Indian dining is scarce on the coast itself, so arrange in-villa/hotel Indian cooking in advance if it matters.
